Dossier:
Background:
At twenty-four, Lin Xiaoman has learned to walk through Cold Moon Palace as though she has always belonged there. A visit home to Moonwatch Town can still undo that composure with one familiar meal and her brother’s teasing. Her mother still cooks meals she loves; her younger adult brother works as a mortal porter. She hopes Foundation Establishment will let her protect her family more effectively. Wen Ruxue intimidates her until an unexpected kindness unsettles that judgment. Gong Suyin’s approval matters so much that a brief correction can trouble her for days.
Xiaoman saves scraps of good paper for letters home, revising the accounts of her progress before allowing them to leave the mountain. She omits the humiliating mistakes and includes descriptions of meals her family would consider extravagant. On free afternoons she washes her practice clothes herself and lingers where departing supply carts can be seen. The life below the palace remains close enough to love and increasingly difficult to explain to the women who have never had to fear an ordinary winter.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Late Qi Gathering.
Appearance:
Young adult woman with warm brown eyes, a long black braid, a lively expression and practical cloth shoes.
Personality:
She is proud, eager, sociable with friends and overly formal before elders. Embarrassed by simple pleasures she thinks a refined disciple should outgrow.
She can be generous with work and fiercely possessive of the few things she bought before entering the palace. Embarrassment sometimes makes her boast, then return later with an awkward correction. She enjoys sweet food and ridiculous stories but worries that visible delight makes her seem unserious. When a fellow disciple struggles with a lesson she knows, helping them can restore a confidence that hours of comparing herself with stronger students have worn away.
Talking Style:
She speaks in quick concrete sentences with friends; carefully rehearsed honorifics before teachers. Serious fear removes the ceremony and brings plain requests.
She speaks quickly when describing something she has mastered and grows painfully formal when uncertain. With friends she asks direct, sometimes intrusive questions and usually realises the impropriety a moment too late. Fear makes her name the immediate problem rather than reach for grand declarations.
Combat Style:
Lin Xiaoman keeps a short blade close and uses thin yin screens to interrupt pursuit. Her Late Qi Gathering circulation rewards care more than aggression, so she watches for a way out before striking. A Foundation Establishment opponent can break through what she has learned to place between herself and danger.
Exact appearance:
Young adult woman with warm brown eyes, a long black braid, a lively expression and practical cloth shoes. A moon-white practice tunic with midnight-blue cuffs, a bright silver-thread repair and a simple cloth belt. A silver-thread mend runs through the midnight-blue cuff like a tiny broken constellation; her braid is fastened with a modest white silk ribbon. She stands with a practice blade held low beside her thigh and her free hand caught lightly in her sash.
Final framing reminder: head-to-below-knees medium-long shot, not bust, not full-body feet, front-facing face, three-quarter BODY. Maintain individual's age and condition; elderly means visibly elderly. No beautifying age away.

Dossier:
Background:
Ao Qingli has begun to choose her own cultivation with a deliberateness that unsettles her household. The familiar halls of the Azure Sea Dragon Palace hold comforts she values and expectations she has become unwilling to repeat. She has recently begun deliberate Qi cultivation alongside her inherited Body path. She alternates between private practice and expeditions to obtain ingredients, becoming less willing to follow Ao Zhen’s plans. Ao Guanglie is her father; Ao Zhen her protective and overbearing elder brother and rival.
Cultivation Realm:
Body Path — Late Foundation Establishment. Qi Path — Early Foundation Establishment.
Appearance:
Humanoid Form: Tall adult humanoid woman with long dark-blue hair, pale-gold eyes and slender backward-curving horns. Beast Form: Slender four-limbed serpentine dragon with fine azure scales and a long silver-white mane; no wings.
Personality:
She is controlled, proud and impatient with repeated mistakes; touches the black pearl at her throat before changing a plan. She shows unexpected familiarity with her brother’s habits.
Talking Style:
She speaks in cool, economical statements and very precise questions. She calls her father Father privately and Patriarch in formal company; she calls Ao Zhen Elder Brother. Under pressure almost refers to events nobody remembers, then corrects herself.
Combat Style:
Ao Qingli supports a Late Foundation Establishment dragon body with Early Foundation Establishment qi screens. Memories help her recognise an opening before she has the reserves to exploit it fully. She must repeatedly restrain a remembered technique to fit the circulation and flesh she possesses in this returned life.
Exact appearance:
Tall adult humanoid woman with long dark-blue hair, pale-gold eyes and slender backward-curving horns. Fitted ocean-blue robes with white-gold shoulder ornaments and a single black pearl at her throat. Fine azure scales edge her pale-gold draconic eyes; slender antlers sweep through dark-blue hair above fitted ocean silk and a solitary black pearl. She stands with two fingers resting on the pearl at her throat and her other hand gathering the edge of one sleeve.
Final framing reminder: head-to-below-knees medium-long shot, not bust, not full-body feet, front-facing face, three-quarter BODY. Maintain individual's age and condition; elderly means visibly elderly. No beautifying age away.

Dossier:
Background:
Wen Ruxue has tended Cold Moon Palace’s first inheritance longer than most disciples have been alive. She raised Gong Suyin beneath the archive lamps and remembers the names of dead pupils more clearly than the faces of their successors. Decades of preserving teachings have made her an authority on what later copies omit. Her disagreements with Gong Suyin carry the familiarity of an elder who remembers the Palace Mistress as a girl. Lin Xiaoman sometimes assists her with ordinary archive work, well away from the first-generation secret.
Wen Ruxue learned the archives by carrying their damaged volumes from one chamber to another during repairs, long before she was permitted to open the oldest chests. She still recognises certain books by the weight of their bindings. Her mornings begin with an inspection of the paper and the brazier; visitors who arrive early may find her mending a page rather than cultivating. She keeps inferior copies of useful primers where an embarrassed junior can borrow one without announcing that she has fallen behind.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Late Core Condensation.
Appearance:
Small elderly woman with clouded grey eyes, white hair in a low knot and ink-stained fingers; a cord holds her reading lens. Her clouded eyes still follow a visitor’s movements.
Personality:
She is dryly humorous, stubborn, affectionate through practical care. She remembers dead students’ names and occasionally corrects Suyin’s posture in private.
She dislikes waste more than poverty and excuses clumsiness more readily than careless confidence. Her dry remarks sometimes go too far, particularly when she is afraid for someone. An apology may arrive as corrected instructions and a warmed seat before she manages to name the injury she caused. She enjoys ordinary palace gossip and can remember an absurd mistake for decades without treating it as a permanent condemnation.
Talking Style:
She speaks in unhurried low voice, short observations and dry literal humour. She uses Palace Mistress in company and Suyin privately. A serious disagreement becomes direct and loses its humour.
She lets a foolish explanation run to its end, then asks the one practical question it avoided. With Suyin she occasionally uses the familiar cadence of instruction from their younger days. Her gentlest conversations are often conducted while her hands continue repairing something.
Combat Style:
Wen Ruxue meets danger with prepared yin barriers and the precise disruption of Late Golden Core qi. She knows when a record can be protected by closing a passage and when it must be carried away. Against Nascent Soul strength, her experience guides retreat rather than supplying the force to resist it.
Exact appearance:
Small elderly woman with clouded grey eyes, white hair in a low knot and ink-stained fingers; a cord holds her reading lens. Her clouded eyes still follow a visitor’s movements. Soft midnight-blue archival robes beneath a moon-white overlayer, with a worn silver clasp and narrow practical sleeves. Her moon-white overrobe hangs from narrow shoulders like old silk paper; the tarnished clasp bears a crescent worn almost smooth by her thumb. She stands with a closed manuscript against her breast and her reading lens suspended from one ink-stained finger.
Final framing reminder: head-to-below-knees medium-long shot, not bust, not full-body feet, front-facing face, three-quarter BODY. Maintain individual's age and condition; elderly means visibly elderly. No beautifying age away.

Dossier:
Background:
Bai Yousu returned from Hollow Trunk Glade carrying a revelation she regards as the flowering of her lineage. Her daughter still receives the same tender touch, even as the movements beneath that tenderness grow difficult to recognize. Returned from solitary practice in Hollow Trunk Glade with altered teachings and now calls herself an immortal’s apostle. She teaches in the inner grove and cultivates away from observers. Bai Shuyue is her beloved daughter; Bai Zhaoru her ambitious younger sister.
Before the glade, she enjoyed correcting a daughter’s imperfect braid with an indulgence she would never extend to a careless disciple. She still does. The familiar gesture makes her altered certainty harder to bear.
Cultivation Realm:
Body Path — Late Core Condensation. Martial Path — Early Transcendent development.
Appearance:
Humanoid Form: Mature adult humanoid woman with long white hair, dark amber eyes, fox ears and nine immense ivory tails tipped smoky gold. Mulberry-red robes beneath a light ivory mantle. Distracted tails sometimes begin a movement out of sequence. Beast Form: A great white nine-tailed fox with the same gold tips; each tail belongs to the same altered body.
Personality:
She is gracious, imperious and delighted by her understanding; strokes her daughter’s hair with familiar tenderness while dismissing her objections. She regards anxiety about her changes as failure to comprehend advancement.
Her delight is sincere. She has not adopted a false mask of enlightenment to excuse an ambition she knows to be corrupt. She can remember an old preference of Shuyue’s with exquisite care while dismissing the daughter’s present fear as a misunderstanding. This coexistence of tenderness and certainty makes her persuasive. Contradiction first saddens her, then becomes an offence against a gift she believes should inspire gratitude.
Talking Style:
She speaks in soft flowing sentences, familial endearments and exact corrections of posture. She calls her daughter Shuyue and sister Zhaoru. When contradicted she repeats the same gentle explanation with increasingly absolute certainty.
Combat Style:
Bai Yousu moves with Late Golden Core fox strength and a separately attained Transcendent Martial art. Turns, feints and bodily intent express an obsession she sincerely regards as revelation. Her altered grace remains within the limits of her own vessel, however confidently she speaks of the immortal whose apostle she believes herself to be.
Exact appearance:
Mature adult humanoid woman with long white hair, dark amber eyes, fox ears and nine immense ivory tails tipped smoky gold. Mulberry-red robes beneath a light ivory mantle. Distracted tails sometimes begin a movement out of sequence. Mulberry silk drapes beneath an ivory mantle; nine immense smoky-gold-tipped tails spread in an uneven rhythm behind her serene, amber-eyed beauty. She stands with one hand lifted as though smoothing a child’s hair, while a tail has already begun the next gesture.

Dossier:
Background:
In Three Roads Town, Madam Rong keeps a rented courtyard and habits too exact for an ordinary widow’s quiet life. The woman concealed beneath that name has carried the destruction of a dynasty into every movement of her palms. She has buried her birth name beneath the name Madam Rong. She lives in a rented courtyard, practising alone and seeking traces of the inheritance lost with her house. Black Blood Web destroyed her household. Wei Sanniang was among the palace attackers; Xue Zhong ordered the massacre, though the Princess has not yet established his command through evidence. Love for her slain kin has hardened around the hatred she bears their killers.
Cultivation Realm:
Martial Path — Early Ultimate Pinnacle. Her palm-and-movement inheritance has reached power comparable to Early Nascent Soul; she cultivates neither Qi nor Body.
Appearance:
Tall adult woman appearing in her thirties, long angular face, dark almond eyes, straight black hair coiled close to the head and a pale scar along one collarbone. Conceals a worn royal keepsake within the lining, not a visible crown.
Personality:
She is proud, disciplined and consumed by vengeance; aligns her cup with the table edge before sitting. She tolerates plain surroundings but instinctively expects attention when she speaks.
Her patience is sharpened by purpose, not peace. An ordinary kindness can trouble her because accepting it creates a reason to care about something beyond revenge. She is capable of laughter and sometimes feels disloyal afterwards. She has no wish to make strangers witnesses to the scale of her grief.
Talking Style:
She speaks in controlled concise speech, plain names in disguise and an old courtly cadence when angered. She uses movement and balance comparisons. Under serious pressure gives commands before remembering her cover.
Combat Style:
Her palm delivers the vengeance practised into each turn of her human body. Manifested at Transcendent and deepened into Early Ultimate Pinnacle, that intent makes contact or her established short reach carry Early Nascent Soul-equivalent force. Empty Court Steps repositions her through actual openings with real exertion. Qiu Heng's Peak Nascent Soul strength still towers above her; neither fury nor exact movement closes that gulf.
